title: How To Fill Extra Time Without Losing Control Of Your Class of-your-class/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin addresses the common problem of unplanned extra minutes at the end of a lesson, which he argues cause more behavior trouble than most teachers expect because the perceived freedom of unstructured time invites excitability and silliness. His solution is to treat filler time with the same structure as any planned lesson, using a six-step framework: tell students what the activity is, tell them how it works, explain why it matters, set clear expectations, remind them of the consequence for straying, and pause briefly to build anticipation before beginning. He illustrates the framework with a sample "selfie game" that groups students by shared preferences for a quick photo-pose challenge, noting the format is adaptable to nearly any topic. The core message is that even brief, seemingly unimportant stretches of class time deserve the same intention, structure, and accountability as formal instruction, since consistent excellence is a daily habit rather than an occasional effort.
points: Unplanned extra time at the end of a lesson often triggers more misbehavior than teachers expect, due to perceived freedom.
Filling extra time with the same structure as a planned lesson prevents the excitability that unstructured time invites.
The six-step framework covers what, how, why, expectations, consequences, and a brief pause to build anticipation before starting.
The "selfie game" example — grouping students by preference for a quick photo pose — is adaptable to nearly any topic or grade level.
Treating even brief, seemingly minor stretches of class time with intention reflects a broader habit of pursuing excellence daily.
quotes: The perceived freedom of an unplanned break can cause excitability. It can cause silliness and distraction.
The solution is to fill the extra time with purpose, to send the message that nothing has changed, business is usual, and the bar remains high.

If you stray from these expectations, I will follow our classroom management plan and enforce a consequence.
The one reliable way to avoid the accompanying misbehavior is to fill the time with purpose.
Give them structure, intention, direction, urgency, and a reminder of what is at stake—just like you would for any lesson.
Excellence is a habit and a goal you pursue every minute of every day.
